# Research report — Library room booking

## Executive summary
Members want to book study rooms online; the evidence shows self-service booking cuts no-shows when reminders are sent [S1][S2]. We recommend an online booking service with reminders and automatic release of unclaimed rooms.

## Context and objectives
The brief asks for a way for library members to book study rooms without phoning the desk [S3]. The research had to establish user expectations, comparable services and the accessibility duties that apply.

## Research questions
RQ-1 What do members expect from room booking? RQ-2 What do comparable libraries offer? RQ-3 What accessibility obligations apply?

## Method
Web search of library sector sources, vendor documentation and regulators, 2023-2026; every source was fetched and read before being cited [S4].

## Findings
RQ-1: members expect to see availability and book in under two minutes [S1][S2]. RQ-2: comparable libraries release rooms after 15 minutes without check-in [S5]. RQ-3: public-sector services must meet WCAG 2.2 AA [S4].

## Comparables and alternatives
Phone booking (status quo, "do nothing"), a vendor booking module [S5], or a bespoke service. The vendor module meets most needs at the lowest risk.

## Regulatory, standards and accessibility context
The Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations 2018 require WCAG 2.2 AA conformance for the online service [S4].

## Risks and counter-evidence
Automatic release can frustrate members who arrive late; one study found complaints rose briefly after introduction [S2].

## Limitations
No local usage data was available; demand figures are estimates based on desk logs described in the brief [S3].

## Conclusions and implications for requirements
Requirements should cover availability search, booking, reminders, release of unclaimed rooms and WCAG 2.2 AA conformance [S1][S4][S5].

## Sources
- [S1] Library user survey 2025 — Example Library Association, 2025-03-01. https://libraries.example.org/survey-2025 (accessed 2026-10-01)
- [S2] No-shows in shared spaces — Journal of Facilities, 2024-06-10. https://journal.example.com/no-shows (accessed 2026-10-01)
- [S3] Room booking brief — provided by the owner (brief.md), 2026-10-01.
- [S4] Accessibility requirements for public sector websites — UK Government, 2024-01-15. https://www.gov.example.uk/accessibility (accessed 2026-10-01)
- [S5] Room booking module documentation — Vendor Ltd, 2025-09-01. https://docs.vendor.example.net/rooms (accessed 2026-10-01)
